transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess what brings me in is... well, it's probably not a huge deal, but I've just been having a little trouble lately. I feel like I just can't quite settle in my own body anymore? If that makes sense? 

It's mostly just when I'm supposed to sit quietly and, you know, handle paperwork or sit down to make shared household plans. I just get this... sort of restless feeling, I guess. I'm sorry, I hope I'm explaining that right. Is that the sort of thing you help people with?
Do you feel this restlessness mostly in situations where you need to sit still and focus, like during paperwork or planning, or does it happen in other situations as well?

Um, I think it's mostly just those situations? Like the paperwork and the planning. I haven't really noticed it happening a lot in other places... or at least, I don't think I have? 

Since I'm home during the day, I can usually just keep myself busy with chores and errands, so I'm already up and moving around. It's really not too terrible most of the time! I just... I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be. It's probably completely normal to get a little fidgety when you're forced to do boring tasks, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you're trying to focus on tasks like paperwork, do you also find it hard to stay focused or do you feel like you're constantly needing to move or do something else?

Um, yeah, I guess it's a little bit of both? I mean, I definitely get that urge to move, like I said, but... well, the focus part is a little tricky too. 

It's not that I *can't* focus, you know? I can sit down to read an email about household stuff, or even just try to read a chapter of a book for fun, and I start out completely fine! But then... I don't know, maybe I'm just getting older, but after a few minutes, I'll realize I'm just staring at the same paragraph over and over. Like, my eyes are reading the words, but none of it is actually going into my brain? 

I feel so silly admitting that. It's probably just normal fatigue, right? Like, everyone gets a little distracted sometimes? I just try to push through it, but it does make things take a lot longer than they probably should. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you what you need.
Do you ever experience this restlessness or difficulty focusing in other situations, like when you're trying to relax and watch TV, or when you're talking with someone and need to stay attentive?

Um, well, watching TV is usually okay because I can fold laundry or knit while I watch, so I'm doing something. But... I guess if I'm trying to do something really quiet, it can be a little hard. 

Like, sometimes I just want to have a nice, quiet evening reading next to my husband on the couch. That sounds so lovely and relaxing, right? But... I don't know, I always end up kind of ruining the mood, I guess. I'll start humming without realizing it, or I'll suddenly remember something I meant to tell him and just start talking, or I'll keep getting up to grab a glass of water or adjust the thermostat. 

It's really nothing major, just little things! But I make just enough noise or movement that it stops being a peaceful, quiet time. I feel so bad because I know he just wants to relax after work, and I'm over there being a nuisance. I try really hard to just sit still and be quiet, but it just sort of happens? Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not wasting your time with silly little habits like that.
When you're trying to focus or sit still, do you ever feel a sense of internal worry or nervousness that makes it hard to stay calm, or is it more of a physical restlessness without much anxiety?

Um, I don't really think it's an anxious thing? At least, I don't feel worried or nervous when it happens. It's more just... a physical need to move, I guess? Like my body just has too much energy and doesn't know what to do with it. 

I mean, I don't feel stressed about it, really! It's just sort of this... buzzing feeling, if that makes sense? I hope that's okay, that I don't feel anxious about it. I know some people get really stressed when they can't sit still, but for me, it's just... physical, I suppose. Does that make sense? Am I explaining that right?
Looking back, were you also someone who had trouble sitting still or staying focused when you were a child, or does this restlessness mostly seem to have started more recently in your life?

Um, well, it's definitely not a new thing. I guess... looking back, it's kind of always been there? Even way back in elementary school. 

I was always the little girl with the incredibly messy desk, you know? And I'd always forget to bring my permission slips home, or lose them on the way. I remember my teachers would send notes home to my parents saying I was a sweet girl, but that I talked out of turn a lot, or that I just couldn't seem to stay in my seat when I was supposed to. 

I know that sounds terrible, like I was a really bad kid, but I promise I wasn't trying to be disruptive! I just... I don't know, I guess I had a lot of energy back then too. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a nightmare to teach. I really tried to be good! Does that... is that helpful for what you're trying to figure out?
